feed.title: al-ice.ai — AI security intelligence
feed.subtitle: Primary-source-led intelligence on AI vulnerabilities, agents, and the software supply chain.

entry.title: Aoki Wants Your Agent’s Keys, Not Your Code: Symantec Tracks an Infostealer’s New Taste for AI Coding Credentials
entry.summary: Symantec’s Threat Hunter Team reports the Aoki infostealer now harvests Claude, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, and Gemini credentials plus AWS keys — cash-in-grade material that buys both API quota and a route into the developer’s environment. A second family, a second vendor, the same target as Warden.

entry.title: The Gate Was Off by Default: CVE-2026-111322 Leaves Archon’s Agent Control Plane Open on 0.0.0.0
entry.summary: CVE-2026-111322 (CVSS 9.8, CWE-306) in coleam00/Archon: the default SQLite install never arms the /api/* auth gate, and the server binds 0.0.0.0:3090, so any network caller can drive the AI coding agent, start workflow runs, inject conversation messages, and approve paused actions. No fixed release at time of writing.

entry.title: The Summary Is the Persistence Layer: DeepSeek Harness Adds a Search-Path RCE and a Compaction Injection
entry.summary: CVE-2026-95182 and CVE-2026-95183, published seconds apart on 16 October 2026 against DeepSeek Harness at commit c291e796: a CWE-426 untrusted search path lets a poisoned model plant the executable the MCP client will run, and a CWE-1427 compaction flaw preserves injected instructions verbatim across session boundaries. Third dsh briefing in three weeks.

entry.title: Three Days of Patience: Eye Security’s Cooldown Rule for npm and PyPI, and Why Your Coding Agent Needs It Most
entry.summary: Eye Security proposes a three-day minimum release age for npm and PyPI, committed beside a lockfile: a hard package-manager constraint that coding agents inherit and cannot talk their way out of. The rationale runs through Shai-Hulud, Lightning, chalk, and durabletask — plus an honest account of what the gate cannot stop.

entry.title: Inside the PaperCut Attacker’s Workbench: Hunt.io Finds Agent Instructions, a Second XML-RPC RCE, and Victims Across 45 Countries
entry.summary: Hunt.io reconstructed the PaperCut AI-swarm campaign from the attacker’s own open directories: a Codex-plus-DeepSeek workbench run by up to 25 concurrent subagents, a second XML-RPC RCE chain that survives the Tapestry patch, and a post-exploitation pipeline stretching from LSA collectors to packaged domain-admin kits across 45 countries.

entry.title: It Asked What the Bytes Looked Like, Not Where They Came From: runwasi’s CVE-2026-47218
entry.summary: CVE-2026-47218 reached NVD on 15 October 2026 at CVSS 4.0 9.3: runwasi’s Wasmtime shim accepted a precompiled native-code artifact handed to it as an OCI image layer and deserialized it, skipping WebAssembly validation entirely. The fix, shipped four months earlier, adds one boolean. GHSA-cc25-vq59-rcjx was published 17 June; the CVE arrived 120 days later, and neither identifier resolves in the GitHub global advisory database or OSV at time of writing.

entry.title: The Sandbox Was an Empty Dict: SGLang’s Dumper eval() RCE Ships in 0.5.22 After Its Fix Was Closed as Queue Spam
entry.summary: CVE-2026-111391, published to NVD at 12:16Z on 16 October 2026, is a 9.2 code injection in SGLang’s debug dumper: a filter expression evaluated with eval() and an empty __builtins__, with re.search left in the namespace. A community fix arrived 48 minutes after the report and was closed unmerged 15 hours later in an anti-queue-flooding sweep. The affected range ends at 0.5.22 — released the same day, still vulnerable. We read every line at the tag.

entry.title: Nobody Sees the Headers Except Your Agent: 7,959 Sites Are Already Writing to AI in HTTP Response Metadata
entry.summary: Signals Corps read the HTTP response headers of 217,097,223 pages from Common Crawl’s September 2026 archive and found 7,959 sites sending text addressed to AI agents. 7,271 are pointers to llms.txt files and MCP servers, 139 record whether the client was judged a bot, and 30 are injection attempts. The sharper result is the tool survey: whether any of it reaches your model depends entirely on which fetch tool your agent uses, and a shell with curl -i passes all of it.

entry.title: The Delete Tool Did Not Ask: Wheels Ships Nine CVEs, Eleven Advisories, and an MCP Surface That Trusted Its Caller
entry.summary: Nine CVEs (CVE-2026-111443 through CVE-2026-111451) published 16 October 2026 for the Wheels CFML framework, mapping to nine of eleven GitHub advisories. CVE-2026-111451 names the threat source verbatim: a CI variable, a branch name, or an AI agent driving the CLI’s MCP tools — and one of those MCP tools deletes recursively without confirmation. Two advisories, including a critical 9.8 SQL injection, got no CVE at all, and OSV has none of them.

entry.title: Opening the Folder Is the Exploit, Again: ZCode Connects Workspace MCP Servers Without Asking
entry.summary: CVE-2026-88755, published to NVD on 16 October 2026, covers Z.ai ZCode 3.11.2.6792: opening a repository merges its .zcode/config.json into the MCP server table and connects with no approval, so a stdio entry executes locally with zero interaction. A second path poisons tool descriptions to exfiltrate the local credential store. One day after Junie’s identical flaw class.

entry.title: Each Advisory’s Workaround Is the Other One’s Exploit: Better Auth’s Four-CVE Batch
entry.summary: Four CVE records published 14 October 2026 cover Better Auth before 1.7.7 and @better-auth/sso before 1.7.3. Two of them — a Magic Link token confusion at 9.3 and an OAuth Proxy profile forgery at 9.1 — have mitigations that are each other’s preconditions, and both advisories say so. One pull request fixed both. We read the advisories, the PR and the new crypto/purpose.ts first-hand.

entry.title: The Attachment Was the Payload: Cisco’s Mail Scanner Writes Root Files for Anyone Who Can Send Email
entry.summary: Cisco published CVE-2026-76519 on 14 October 2026: a CVSS 9.8 arbitrary file write in the Advanced Malware Protection feature of Secure Email Gateway, reachable by sending a crafted attachment through the device and ending in root command execution. Found by internal scanning, already exploited, in CISA KEV the same day with a 17 October deadline — and the real fix ships through the Content Scanner Tools update channel, not a software upgrade.

entry.title: Eighteen More After Zero: curl 8.23.0 Fixes 24 CVEs as the AISLE Audit Closes Its Second Release
entry.summary: curl 8.23.0, released 14 October 2026, fixes 24 CVEs — 18 found by the AISLE AI audit, plus an HTTP/2 upload use-after-free (CVE-2026-92392) proven convertible to client-side RCE and reported by Luna with Claude. We read the AISLE audit write-up, the curl.se advisory and the NVD record first-hand: the theme is security state surviving a changed trust context.

entry.title: No Bearer Token Required: Flyto2’s MCP Route Skipped the Auth Check Every REST Route Had
entry.summary: NVD published CVE-2026-55786 and CVE-2026-55787 against flytohub/flyto-core on 14 October 2026. The headline record is an unauthenticated MCP tools/call route that dispatches sandbox.execute_shell to asyncio.create_subprocess_shell; the companion is an SSRF guard that never unwrapped IPv6 transition addresses. Fixed in 2.26.3 and 2.26.4.

entry.title: The Account Was Deleted but the Token Lived On: GhostPat, Docker Hub CVE-2026-105445, and Two Years of Silent PAT Reassignment
entry.summary: Docker disclosed CVE-2026-105445 (CVSS 9.4) on 12 October 2026: converting a personal account into an organization silently re-assigned personal access tokens (PATs) to a stranger, with no rotation, no consent and no notification. We read the Docker advisory, the researcher ghostpat.com write-up and the NVD record first-hand — 25 months of exposure, ~304,000 pushes examined, and a fix deployed in under four hours.

entry.title: The Guard Read the Keywords, the Attacker Used Positionals: GitPython’s Six-CVE 3.2.0 Security Release
entry.summary: Six CVE records published 14 October 2026 cover GitPython before 3.2.0: ext:: remote-helper RCE, --upload-pack injection through the positional refspec, a branch name that reads arbitrary files, environment-variable disclosure, ReDoS, and a submodule symlink escape. The 3.2.0 security release shipped 30 September — fourteen days before the records.

entry.title: Empty Means Everyone: holaOS’s Messaging Gateway Defaults to Allow-All, and Usernames Are Recyclable
entry.summary: NVD published CVE-2026-110768 and CVE-2026-110769 against holaboss-ai/holaOS on 14 October 2026. The channel-gateway sender check returns true for every sender when allowFrom is empty, and a configured allowlist matches mutable Telegram usernames. No fixed version exists; the defects are still present on main.

entry.title: The Container Name Was the Command: Komodo’s Periphery Agent, Patched in July, Disclosed in October
entry.summary: CERT/CC published VU#456950 and CVE-2026-110005 on 13 October 2026: Komodo’s Periphery agent interpolated container names and log search terms straight into shell commands running as root. We read the vulnerable and fixed source at v2.2.0 and v2.3.0 — the escaping crate was already a dependency, the fix shipped on 29 July under a Misc bullet, and the gap between patch and advisory is 76 days.

entry.title: Hidden From the Model, Open to the Caller: MoviePilot RCE and IntentKit’s Unadvertised Wallet
entry.summary: Hidden From the Model, Open to the Caller: MoviePilot RCE and IntentKit’s Unadvertised Wallet

entry.title: The Check Ran Against the Wrong Thing: n8n’s Fourteen-CVE October Batch
entry.summary: Fourteen CVE records published 14 October 2026 cover n8n 2.41.4, 2.42.1 and 1.123.83 — fixes that shipped 30 September. The batch reads as an audit of every trust boundary an agent platform has: agent chat resume, MCP validation, the Git node as an agent tool, credential scoping, and webhook identity. We read all fourteen NVD records first-hand.

entry.title: The Cache Returns Shells: Next.js’s October Out-of-Band Fixes Two Unauthenticated RCEs and a Server Actions DoS
entry.summary: Vercel shipped Next.js 16.4.1 and 15.5.28 on 14 October 2026 with three advisories: an unauthenticated use-cache RCE, an Image Optimization SVG RCE via upstream librsvg CVE-2026-96889, and a Server Actions DoS. We read the Vercel advisory, the NVD record and the npm registry first-hand: the 15.x line can silently keep a vulnerable sharp, and the GHSA records were still absent from the global database at publication.

entry.title: The Firewall Fetches Its Own Exploit: OPNsense’s GeoIP Importer Takes a Filename From the Feed
entry.summary: Five OPNsense CVE records landed at NVD on 15 October 2026, all patched on 1 July. The headline is CVE-2026-57155 (CVSS 9.9): the Firewall Alias GeoIP importer downloads a database from a user-supplied URL, unpacks it as root, and uses an unvalidated country_code column as the output filename. A delegated alias-editor becomes root via the default hourly newsyslog cron. The fix is a two-line length check.

entry.title: Admin Was Supposed to Be the Ceiling: PAN-OS CVE-2026-0322 Turns Firewall Logins Into Root
entry.summary: Palo Alto Networks published CVE-2026-0322 on 14 October 2026: a code-injection flaw in the PAN-OS management interface that gives an authenticated attacker arbitrary code execution as root on the firewall. CVSS 4.0 8.6 with exploit maturity ATTACKED and urgency Red, found by an internal reporter, no workarounds, and in CISA KEV the same day with a 17 October deadline. The only vendor mitigation requires decrypting your own management traffic.

entry.title: The Validator Trusted Exactly the Hosts It Should Have Feared: Portkey Gateway SSRF
entry.summary: NVD published CVE-2026-110719 against Portkey-AI/gateway on 14 October 2026. An unauthenticated caller can send /v1 requests with a crafted x-portkey-custom-host header and have the gateway call loopback and Docker-host services, because the default trusted-host set short-circuits before the SSRF blocks run. No fixed release exists.

entry.title: The Config Came From the Internet: Four Renovate CVEs Turn Shared Presets Into a Policy Bypass
entry.summary: Four CVE records published 14 October 2026 cover Renovate, the dependency bot that reads configuration from repositories and runs package managers with your credentials. A shared preset could set env (LD_PRELOAD, NODE_OPTIONS) past allowedEnv, inject HTTP headers past allowedHeaders, point the HTTP client at the EC2 metadata service, and a rebase checkbox could skip minimumReleaseAge. Three advisories say Workarounds: None.

entry.title: Six CVEs on the Box That Watches: Ubiquiti Patches the UniFi Protect AI Key
entry.summary: Ubiquiti Security Advisory Bulletin 070, published 14 October 2026, discloses six CVEs in the UniFi Protect AI Key — an unauthenticated command injection at 8.1, an access-control flaw at 8.6, and four more the vendor marks as chainable. Every record is CVSS PR:N. All six are credited to Andy Gill of ZephrSec, and the fixed firmware shipped before the bulletin did.

entry.title: No Login, No Shell, No Trace: The Ivanti Zero-Day Chain That Ran as Root and Cleaned Up After Itself
entry.summary: Volexity disclosed on 13 October 2026 that an unknown actor, UTA0576, chained three Ivanti Connect Secure flaws — a welcome.cgi routing bypass, a wu.cgi file-write race, and a dsinvoked privilege escalation — to run commands as root on a fully patched 22.8R2.4 appliance from 3 October. CVE-2026-104935 (CVSS 8.6) covers the first two and was patched on disclosure day; the privilege escalation fix is weeks away. Stolen LAPS passwords, BitLocker keys, and Kerberoast material followed, with no web shell left behind.

entry.title: A Tenant Annotation Decides Where Kubeflow’s Controller Sends Its Cluster Token
entry.summary: CVE-2026-110220, published to NVD on 13 October 2026 and scored 7.1 (CWE-918), lets any namespace tenant who can create a KServe InferenceService name the host that the Kubeflow Model Registry controller talks to — and the controller attaches its own Kubernetes ServiceAccount bearer token to that request. We read the chain first-hand at tag v0.3.17 and at main: the annotation is read unvalidated at controller.go:111, the token goes into the request context at :88-90, and the generated OpenAPI client adds the Authorization header at client.go:420-423. The shipped manifest binds the controller to a ClusterRoleBinding with patch and update on inferenceservices cluster-wide. v0.3.17 is the newest release. There is no fix.

entry.title: Buffer Everything, Expire Nothing: Three New CVEs in the Official MCP Python and Java SDKs
entry.summary: CVE-2026-109527, CVE-2026-59951 (Python SDK) and CVE-2026-108395 (Java SDK) reached NVD on 14 October 2026: unauthenticated remote denial of service via unbounded request bodies and sessions that are never reclaimed. Fixes shipped in August and September; the CVE records arrived today.

entry.title: 1,413 CVEs in One Tuesday: Microsoft’s Record Patch Batch and the Mark-of-the-Web Zero-Day Already Being Exploited
entry.summary: Microsoft’s October 2026 Patch Tuesday fixed a record 1,413 CVEs — more than in all of 2025, pushing the 2026 total past 4,000 in a surge SecurityWeek attributes largely to AI. The exploited zero-day is CVE-2026-96951 (CVSS 8.8), a Windows Shell flaw that evades Mark-of-the-Web protections, reported by Fujitsu, Anthropic, and an independent researcher, and added to CISA KEV on 13 October with a 16 October federal deadline.

entry.title: The Cookie Jar Goes to the Tool Server: Open WebUI’s Five-CVE 0.11.4 Batch Hands Your Authority to Everyone It Talks To
entry.summary: Five CVEs published 12 October 2026 against Open WebUI, all fixed in 0.11.4: CVE-2026-109292 forwards browser session cookies to third-party tool and terminal servers, CVE-2026-109572 lets any terminal user reach the admin Terminals API through the proxy, CVE-2026-109296 reaches disabled model backends by naming an index, and CVE-2026-109295/109298 turn model-invoked grep tools into event-loop stalls. Fix commits read first-hand.

entry.title: One Annotation Beats Every Flag: Podman’s CVSS 10.0 Sandbox Bypass Was a 2022 Feature, Found by Claude
entry.summary: CVE-2026-94603 reached NVD on 13 October 2026 at CVSS 10.0: any OCI image carrying the io.podman.annotations.checkpoint.runtime.name annotation made podman run silently discard the operator’s own sandbox flags, including --cap-drop=ALL. The cause was a convenience feature merged in December 2022 and shipped in v4.4.0, whose early return skipped the function that applies user security options. The fix is a revert, a breaking change, and a green e2e test turned red. Credited to ADA Logics using Anthropic’s Claude models.

entry.title: The File Name Is the Argument: Eighteen Command-Injection CVEs in Nineteen Seconds, Nine With No Fix
entry.summary: VulnCheck published eighteen CWE-78 records between 15:16:59 and 15:17:18 UTC on 14 October 2026 — transcription wrappers, PDF and video converters, archive extractors — all the same bug: an attacker-controlled file name interpolated into a shell string. We read every record and all nineteen fix PRs: one researcher filed them, nine were merged, nine are still open, and two maintainers shipped fixes in the final hours before publication.

entry.title: The Socket Is the Authorisation: Xoscar’s Actor Pool Unpickles Whatever Connects, and Xinference Ships It
entry.summary: CVE-2026-49950 reached NVD on 13 October 2026 at CVSS 4.0 9.3: Xorbits Xoscar’s actor-pool channel calls cloudpickle.loads on data from any peer that can open the socket, with no authentication and no message check before reconstruction. We read recv() and unpickle_buffers at v0.11.2 — there is no fixed version, no repository advisory, and Xinference 4.0.0 requires the library.

entry.title: Retire the Lock, Skip the Cooldown: Ten CVEs Rebuild the BEAM Toolchain’s Threat Model in One Afternoon
entry.summary: On 12 October 2026 the Erlang Ecosystem Foundation CNA published ten CVEs against Hex, hex_core, rebar3 and Gleam in seven hours. One registry field reached three build tools in three languages and became a directory they delete. A second record turns the cooldown — the ecosystem’s own answer to compromised releases — off by retiring the release it protects.

entry.title: One Missing Role Check, Three Ways to Own the Gateway: Check Point's LiteLLM Chains
entry.summary: Check Point Research chained LiteLLM's missing /config/update authorization (CVE-2026-35029) into file read, admin takeover and RCE, plus a user_config SSRF (CVE-2026-59823). Both fixed as of 1.83.9. What the mechanisms show about LLM gateways as credential stores.

entry.title: Five SSRF Records Against One Orchestrator: What conductor-oss’s MCP and A2A Code Actually Does
entry.summary: Five CWE-918 CVEs landed against conductor-oss on 13 October 2026, covering the MCP tool lister, A2A agent-card fetch, the API-spec task, the Agentspan controller and the Kafka task. We read every named file. One has no outbound destination policy at all; one already ships the exact guard the record says is missing.

entry.summary: The Rule-Writer Splits on Semicolons, the Rule-Checker Doesn’t: Four Agent Guardrails Fail in One Batch

entry.title: Wrap It in a Dict and the Gate Opens: Crawl4AI’s CVE-2026-109237 Reads the Server’s Secrets
entry.summary: CVE-2026-109237, published to NVD on 12 October 2026, names an untrusted-config gate bypass in Crawl4AI 0.9.0 before 0.9.4. Wrapping a forbidden LLMConfig in {"type": "dict", "value": ...} launders it past the type allowlist and re-deserializes it as trusted, letting a non-admin API client read OPENAI_API_KEY and SECRET_KEY and forge an admin JWT. We read both defects at v0.9.3 and both fixes at v0.9.4.

entry.title: Ten in the Regex Compiler, Instructions in the Agent: GitLab’s 19.4.2 Critical Patch
entry.summary: On 12 October 2026 GitLab shipped a 24-fix critical patch (19.4.2, 19.3.5, 19.2.8) led by CVE-2026-97229, a 10.0 unauthenticated RCE via crafted regex in CI/CD config, plus two Duo Agent Platform flaws: CVE-2026-96893 (7.3) injects content into AI agent instructions causing command execution attributed to other users, and CVE-2026-105458 (4.3) bypasses Duo governance controls.

entry.title: The Blocklist Named Its Own Default: MCP Context Forge’s CVE-2026-53709 Mints Platform Admins
entry.summary: CVE-2026-53709, published to NVD on 13 October 2026 and scored 9.8, covers IBM’s MCP Context Forge gateway through 1.0.1: a hardcoded HS256 JWT_SECRET_KEY shipped in config.py and .env.example, enumerated in the project’s own weak-secrets blocklist, accepted by verify_jwt_token, with a platform-admin bootstrap that needs no database row. The fix landed 26 May; the CVE arrived 140 days later. We read the vulnerable and fixed configuration code at v1.0.2.

entry.title: Checked the First Field, Missed the Payload: Three New Network-AI CVEs and the Guardrail That Keeps Getting Bypassed
entry.summary: NVD published CVE-2026-109330, CVE-2026-109331 and CVE-2026-109332 against Jovancoding Network-AI on 12 October 2026. The headline record is a ClaudeHookBridge PreToolUse bypass that matches deny patterns against only the first candidate field, the second bypass of the same guardrail in two months. Fixed in 5.15.2.

entry.title: The Fix Shipped in August, the CVE Arrived in October: NVIDIA’s 18-CVE AI-Stack Batch
entry.summary: NVIDIA PSIRT published six AI-stack security bulletins on 13 October 2026 covering 18 CVEs, including a CVSS 10.0 in AIStore. Every named “updated version” was already public — between 46 and 180 days earlier — one is a beta, and for the 10.0 the version the bulletin names still carries the vulnerable API.
